settings.title: Heating type and regulation
settings.description: The settings that belong to this thermostat. The heating type comes first: a water type uses the water data and the boiler's call ("Water and boiler"); not set, SmartPI reads neither. With "Use the SmartPI defaults" on, the shared regulator settings come from the "SmartPI defaults" entry; off, the next step sets this thermostat's own values.

data.smart_pi_allow_pwm_cycle_force: Allow PWM cycle restart on band transitions

data_description.minimal_activation_delay: SmartPI's own: Versatile Thermostat's TPI delay is not used. 0: no delay.
data_description.smart_pi_use_defaults: Off: this thermostat keeps its own values of the shared settings (they start as a copy of the defaults).

settings_own.title: This thermostat's regulator settings
settings_own.description: This thermostat's own values of the settings shared in "SmartPI defaults". A change in the defaults does not reach them.

data.smart_pi_deadband_allow_p: Allow damped P near deadband edge

heating_inputs.title: Water and boiler
heating_inputs.description: Where SmartPI reads the water that reaches this thermostat's emitters, and whether the boiler is called for heat. Use entities of any integration (for example a temperature sensor on the supply pipe), or an integration that implements SmartPI's contract (a provider): it is listed here once installed. See SmartPI's documentation, "Water and boiler inputs" (documentation/en/water_input.md).

data_description.smart_pi_water_source: With the supply water temperature SmartPI knows how much heat a command brings. None: SmartPI works without it.
data_description.smart_pi_boiler_call_source: Whether the boiler heats while this zone calls for heat: SmartPI does not learn from heat that does not come. None: SmartPI takes every command for heat.

data_description.smart_pi_supply_entity: The temperature of the water that reaches this thermostat's circuit (after its mixing valve, if it has one).
data_description.smart_pi_boiler_signals: Take the boiler's signals from SmartPI defaults, or set this thermostat's own.

heating_signals.title: This thermostat's boiler signals
heating_signals.description: All are optional: leave a field empty if you have no such entity.

data_description.smart_pi_heat_available_entity: On while the boiler can heat the circuits now.
data_description.smart_pi_dhw_entity: On while the boiler heats the domestic hot water instead of the circuits.
data_description.smart_pi_fault_entity: On while the boiler reports a fault.

zone.title: Zone with two heat sources

zone_master.title: Zone with two heat sources: master thermostat
zone_master.description:
A zone heated by two thermostats with SmartPI (for example a radiator and an underfloor loop) is set up from its master thermostat: a Versatile Thermostat over climate whose two devices are these thermostats. The master holds the setpoint, presets, schedule, mode and windows of the zone and passes them to both.

The master must have self-regulation off and exactly two devices, both Versatile Thermostats with SmartPI, measuring the zone with the same temperature sensor, and neither may already belong to another zone. Recommended on the master: a long safety delay (its safety mode switches both devices off) and a small regulation threshold step.

neighbour_add.title: Add a neighbouring zone
neighbour_add.description: Choose the Versatile Thermostat or the temperature sensor of the neighbouring zone.

data.neighbour_window_action: When the neighbour's window is open

data_description.mode: Always: the zones share their air. When a door is open: the exchange follows the door sensors. None: keep the neighbour on the list but ignore it.
data_description.door_sensors: Doors between the two zones; the connection is open while any of them is open. Window sensors stay in the window detection of Versatile Thermostat.
data_description.neighbour_window_action: Applied while the connection is open and the neighbour thermostat reports an open window.

dependency_remove.title: Remove neighbouring zones
dependency_remove.description: Nothing chosen: back to the menu.

model_reset.title: Reset the learned model
model_reset.description: These changes affect what SmartPI has learned: {reasons}. Resetting clears SmartPI's whole learned model of the thermostats concerned (for a zone, the main source's) so that they learn again from the start; it is recommended. If you keep the model after a change of the water data, SmartPI does not ask again when these data start.

source_menu.title: Additional source of a zone

source_role.title: Additional source of a zone
source_role.description: This thermostat works as the additional source of the zone set up in {main}: it applies the commands of that zone's main source, and its own regulation and learning are paused. The zone's settings are in that entry. Here are the settings that still apply: its heating type, its cycle's delays and, for a valve, its curve. Its other regulator settings keep their values and apply only when it regulates on its own because the main source has gone silent.

water_data_appeared.title: Water temperature data are now available for {name}

confirm.title: Reset the learned model of {name}?
confirm.description: SmartPI now receives the supply water temperature of this thermostat from the water data source, so its heating power is measured at a reference water temperature. The power learned before does not match these units. Resetting lets SmartPI learn the room again (recommended).

water_data_gone.title: Water temperature data are no longer available for {name}

confirm.title: Reset the learned model of {name}?
confirm.description: The supply water temperature of this thermostat's circuit no longer comes from the water data source, so SmartPI works without it. The power learned at a reference water temperature does not match these units. Resetting lets SmartPI learn the room again (recommended).

thermostat_entries_created.title: SmartPI created an entry of its own for some thermostats
thermostat_entries_created.description: The "SmartPI defaults" entry no longer holds the settings that belong to one thermostat (heating type, activation delays, valve curve, PWM cycle restart). These thermostats ran with such settings from the defaults, so each one now has its own SmartPI entry with them: {entries}. They use the shared settings of the defaults as before. Check each entry's options if a thermostat needs other values.
